risks: Minimal: no intervention; risks are to privacy of student-level data and to families asked to show vaccination cards.
consent: Branch A uses register data under the custodian's authority without individual consent, subject to its decision. Branch B asks parents for permission to check cards at school, with an opt-out form translated into the main home languages; students may decline.
data: No names leave the register or the school; outputs are aggregated so that no cell has fewer than ten students.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: place of residence (neighbourhood deprivation), language spoken at home and socioeconomic position are the central stratifiers; consent materials and reminders are translated.
effectiveness: Shows where next year's program should go.
efficiency: Uses existing data or a small survey.
costs: Translation of the survey permission form; nurse time within school hours.
partnerships: School board research committee, school principals, the register custodian and two parent representatives from schools with low consent return.
rebPath: Public health program evaluation reviewed by the district's research ethics committee; school board research committee approval required before any in-school data collection (next meeting 2026-11-18).
limitations: Design undecided until data access is resolved; ecological stratifiers.
summary: Low-risk evaluation whose ethical path differs by branch; translated materials and aggregated outputs protect families.
